messages:
Alex C.: Thinking about short-term spikes — proposing we add a "burst penalty decay" layer on top of token buckets. idea: when an org drains its burst credit we immediately reduce refill rate by X% for Y seconds instead of hard-blocking. that lets low-volume retries proceed and avoids mass 429 storms.

Sasha P.: hmm, so soft-throttle first, hard-block later? sounds reasonable. how do we prevent one noisy key from dragging the whole org down? per-key isolation?

Alex C.: per-key buckets still, but penalty is hierarchical: key penalty + org penalty. key penalty decays faster (e.g., 30s), org penalty decays slower (e.g., 5m). config proposal below.

Jun P.: can you paste the config? want to see interactions with short-window burst credits and long-window quotas.

Alex C.: sure — prototype config:
```
burst_policy:
  bucket_capacity: 100
  refill_per_sec: 2
  penalty_on_drain:
    immediate_refill_mult: 0.2  # reduce refill to 20%
    key_decay_secs: 30
    org_decay_secs: 300
    fallback_model: "gpt-lite-v1"
```
This also triggers an immediate routing fallback (same request switched to fallback_model) for the portion of tokens that would exceed capacity.

Liz M.: UX q: if we auto-fallback to a cheaper model, do we surface that in the Console/req logs and in the SDK response metadata? we need customers to see when quality changed.

Alex C.: yes — plan: add header `X-Redwood-Fallback: gpt-lite-v1` and console badge on request-level timeline + per-route metric.

Sasha P.: fair. on fairness: what about burst transfer from high-traffic keys to low-traffic keys in same org? if org penalty is applied, low-traffic keys would also get limited. is that acceptable?

Alex C.: that's the tradeoff. option A = conservative org penalty (low reduction, longer decay). option B = only apply org penalty after N offending keys detected in sliding window. leaning B.

Jun P.: telemetry: we need new metrics + traces: `burst.penalty_applied`, `burst.penalty_level`, `fallback.routed`, `fallback.latency_delta`. Also capture `pre_penalty_bucket` and `post_penalty_bucket` sizes for debugging.

quota-bot: auto-note: created alert `BurstPenaltyRate > 10/min` in #eng-sre when more than 10 penalties occur per minute org-wide.

Liz M.: rollout UX: default OFF for existing orgs, opt-in for new orgs? or ship a canary to 10% orgs and collect quality/regression metrics?

Alex C.: canary sounds right. deploy plan: 1) lab env + synthetic load test 2) 1% canary across different org sizes 3) 10% with telemetry dashboards locked 4) global opt-in. add kill-switch per-org in Console.

Sasha P.: ops question: how do we surface emergency rollback in the console? we need a per-org toggle and a global kill switch. also audit log entry when penalty toggled.

Alex C.: agree. Console components: per-org toggle + global `disable_penalty` flag. audit logs + metrics emitted when toggled.

Jun P.: small perf note: adding penalties to hot path must be cheap (few atomic ops). avoid datastore calls per request — keep in local memcache + async persistence.

Alex C.: yep using local shard cache + background sync to central quota store; also add jitter to decay timers to avoid sync storms.

ops-bot: incident-detect: observed 7 penalty events in last 5m for org `alpha-inc`. auto-create ticket? :eyes:

Liz M.: action items: (1) Alex to write design doc with config semantics + canary plan, (2) Jun to mock telemetry + dashboards, (3) Sasha to review fairness thresholds, (4) Product to draft Console UX copy.

Alex C.: I'll prod a doc today and drop link. thanks all. :thumbsup:
